source_text: Ave gratia plena, fons lucis, qui cunctos in ipsum credentes illuminat. Ave gratia plena, intelligibilis solis oriens, et flos vitae immaculatus. Ave gratia plena, pratum fragrantissimum. Ave gratia plena, vitis semper vigens; quae animas glorificantium te laetificas. Ave gratia plena, ager qui non exaratus fructus profert pulcherrimos: Secundum naturam quidem, eo quod more nostro, et tempore motus, gestationisque servato protulisti: at praeter naturam, aut potius supra naturam; quia superne divinum Verbum advenit, et in sancto tuo utero Adamum reformavit. Ac fecunditatem quidem, Spiritus Sanctus sanctae virgini praebuit: verum autem corpus ex eius corpore assumptum est.
thought_title: Hail to Mary as light and fruitful field
orientation: The homily continues praising Mary with a series of greetings after Gabriel announces the conception to her.
pass_a_gloss: Hail full of grace, fount of light, who illuminates all believing in him. Hail full of grace, rising of the intelligible sun, and undefiled flower of life. Hail full of grace, most fragrant meadow. Hail full of grace, vine always thriving; you who gladden the souls of those glorifying you. Hail full of grace, field which not plowed brings forth most beautiful fruits: according to nature indeed, in that in our manner, and with the time of motion and of gestation having been kept you brought forth: but beyond nature, or rather above nature; because from above the divine Word came, and in your holy womb reformed Adam. And fecundity indeed, the Holy Spirit furnished to the holy virgin: but the true body was assumed from her body.

choices.why: keeps noun oriens as rising and intelligibilis as perceived by mind, not visible
immaculatus means without stain, matching spotless sense without adding theology
vigens is being vigorous and alive, semper is temporal always

choices.term: ager qui non exaratus fructus profert pulcherrimos
choices.english: field which not plowed brings forth most beautiful fruits
choices.why: preserves negative relative clause and superlative force without smoothing into untilled
re means again, not first creation but remaking in the womb

pass_b_english: Hail, full of grace, fount of light, who enlightens all who believe in him. Hail, full of grace, rising of the sun known to the mind, and undefiled flower of life. Hail, full of grace, most fragrant meadow. Hail, full of grace, vine always thriving, who fills with joy the souls of those who glorify you.

Hail, full of grace, field never plowed yet bringing forth the most beautiful fruit. By nature you brought forth fruit in our human way, keeping the full time of stirring and bearing. Yet this was beyond nature, or rather above nature, for the divine Word came from above and made Adam anew in your holy womb. The Holy Spirit granted fruitfulness to the holy virgin, and the true body was taken from her body.
